title: What can you say about iodine in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 5 wordings for iodine; the strongest is "Supports normal thyroid function" (strong, 22.5-800 µg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats hypothyroidism, goiter or other thyroid disease".

supported_wordings.why: Listed by Health Canada and authorized in the EU after EFSA review.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 19 and older. Health Canada: 14-800 µg a day. EU: at least 22.5 µg, 15% of the 150 µg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII); its wording is normal production of thyroid hormones and normal thyroid function. ODS upper limit: 1,100 µg.
supported_wordings.form: Iodine from a salt on Health Canada's list (such as potassium iodide), counted as iodine

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Treats hypothyroidism, goiter or other thyroid disease
Fixes a slow or sluggish thyroid

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition
